newsitem.title: UK: UK hallmarking rises sharply in 1996 third quarter.
newsitem.headline: UK hallmarking rises sharply in 1996 third quarter.

text.p: Nearly 6.5 million gold, silver and platinum items were hallmarked in the UK during the 1996 third quarter, the Assay Offices of Great Britain said on Wednesday.
A total of 5,040,483 gold items were hallmarked to show a 16.8 percent increase over the like 1995 period with British-made articles 15.3 percent higher at 3,035,163.
Stamped gold articles made outside of the UK totalled just over two million to record a 19.2 percent increase on the 1995 third quarter total.
Silver hallmarking increased by 11.1 percent to 1,434,937 articles and their weight rose by 14.4 percent to 32,220 kgs.
Platinum articles rose by 109.1 percent to 9,259 articles.
"The marked increase in all standards has been most encouraging," an Assay Office spokesman said.

"The steady but progressive move up-market to the higher carat gold is again evident from the figures, although the nine carat standard continues to dominate sales representing 88 percent of the total gold," he said.
He said the higher silver figures were "beginning to reflect a renewed confidence from the jewellery and allied trades".
